grampians-national-park-1.name: MacKenzie Falls
grampians-national-park-1.bio: Grampians' most iconic waterfall, viewed from a lookout platform or via a steep track down to its base.

grampians-national-park-2.name: The Pinnacle
grampians-national-park-2.bio: Marked walk from Halls Gap up to a lookout over canyons, Halls Gap and the plains.

grampians-national-park-3.name: Grampians Peaks Trail
grampians-national-park-3.bio: A 164 km, 13-day trail from Mt Zero through Halls Gap to Dunkeld, with day-walk sections and hike-in campgrounds.

grampians-national-park-4.name: Boroka Lookout
grampians-national-park-4.bio: Short stroll through stringybark forest to two lookouts over the Halls Gap valley and the plains, golden at sunrise.

grampians-national-park-5.name: The Balconies
grampians-national-park-5.bio: Short walk to a cliff-top lookout over the Victoria Valley, with views of the Grampians ranges.

grampians-national-park-6.name: Reids Lookout
grampians-national-park-6.bio: Lookout in the Grampians ranges with a panorama of the plains and Halls Gap below.

grampians-national-park-7.name: Chautauqua Peak
grampians-national-park-7.bio: Climb to a peak lookout over Halls Gap in the Grampians, with wildlife along the approach track.

grampians-national-park-8.name: Mount William
grampians-national-park-8.bio: Highest peak in Grampians National Park, a challenging walk to a summit with 360 degree views.

grampians-national-park-9.name: Venus Baths
grampians-national-park-9.bio: Easy walk from Halls Gap to natural rockpools fed by Stony Creek, good for a summer cool-off.

grampians-national-park-10.name: Mount Rosea
grampians-national-park-10.bio: Strenuous 8.6 km return walk through messmate forest and past the Gate of the East Wind to a 360-degree summit.

grampians-national-park-11.name: Halls Gap Zoo
grampians-national-park-11.bio: Victoria's largest privately owned regional zoo, with over 120 species, animal encounters and twilight tours.

grampians-national-park-12.name: Gulgurn Manja Aboriginal Rock Art Site
grampians-national-park-12.bio: Rock art shelter near Laharum telling the Jarwadjali story, a short walk from Hollow Mountain car park.

grampians-national-park-13.name: Bunjil Shelter
grampians-national-park-13.bio: Aboriginal rock art shelter near Stawell in Black Range Scenic Reserve, linked to the creator Bunjil.

grampians-national-park-14.name: Manja Shelter
grampians-national-park-14.bio: Short forest walk to a shelter with some of Victoria's best Aboriginal hand stencils and animal tracks.

grampians-national-park-15.name: Ngamadjidj Shelter
grampians-national-park-15.bio: Self-guided walk to an important Aboriginal rock art site, suitable for all fitness levels and prams.

grampians-national-park-17.name: Hollow Mountain
grampians-national-park-17.bio: Steep climb past an iron-stained cliff to wind-scoured caverns and views over the Wimmera Plains.

grampians-national-park-18.name: Mount Abrupt
grampians-national-park-18.bio: Strenuous 6.5 km walk over rock slabs to a lookout with views of the Serra Range and Dunkeld.

grampians-national-park-19.name: Mount Sturgeon
grampians-national-park-19.bio: Summit walk on Wurgarri, the mount behind Dunkeld at the southern end of the Grampians.

grampians-national-park-20.name: Mount Piccaninny
grampians-national-park-20.bio: Walk to Bainggug (Piccaninny) in Grampians National Park, with its own trailhead and a separate West Walk.

grampians-national-park-21.name: Silverband Falls
grampians-national-park-21.bio: Horsetail falls on Dairy Creek, reached by an easy stroll along a fern-lined trail in the Wonderland Range.

grampians-national-park-22.name: Halls Gap
grampians-national-park-22.bio: Fyans Valley town at the foot of the Wonderland Range, home to the Brambuk Aboriginal cultural centre.

grampians-national-park-23.name: Dunkeld
grampians-national-park-23.bio: Town at the southern end of the Grampians where the Grampians Peaks Trail finishes, with a museum and gallery.

grampians-national-park-24.name: Stawell
grampians-national-park-24.bio: Gold-rush town founded in 1853 and home of the Stawell Gift footrace, 10 km north of Bunjil's Shelter rock art.

ararat-1.name: Aradale Lunatic Asylum
ararat-1.bio: Former asylum of up to 70 historic buildings, seen on guided tours on Wednesdays and Sundays at 10am.

ararat-2.name: J Ward
ararat-2.bio: Former county gaol turned psychiatric facility, with daily volunteer-led tours of the cells, chapel and graves.

ararat-3.name: Gum San Chinese Heritage Centre
ararat-3.bio: Museum on the site that began Ararat's gold rush, telling the Chinese miners' voyage to the goldfields.

ararat-4.name: Ararat Gallery TAMA
ararat-4.bio: Textile Art Museum Australia in Ararat's Town Hall, collecting contemporary fibre art since 1968.

ararat-5.name: Seppelt Great Western
ararat-5.bio: Winery from the 1860s at Great Western, with historic underground cellars and early Australian sparkling wines.

ararat-6.name: Langi Ghiran State Park
ararat-6.bio: Park east of Ararat with a short walk to Djab Wurrung rock art and a 10 km climb to views over the plains.

ararat-7.name: Mount Buangor State Park
ararat-7.bio: Forested national park of fern gullies and escarpments, with a waterfalls walk and lookouts over the countryside.

hamilton-victoria-1.name: Hamilton Botanic Gardens
hamilton-victoria-1.bio: Gardens laid out from 1881 by William Guilfoyle, with lakes, fountains and eight trees on the significant trees register.

hamilton-victoria-2.name: Sir Reginald Ansett Transport Museum
hamilton-victoria-2.bio: Museum in Ansett's first hangar on Lake Hamilton, with a Fokker Universal like the one on its 1936 first flight.

hamilton-victoria-3.name: Wannon Falls
hamilton-victoria-3.bio: Punchbowl waterfall on the Wannon River, formed by a basalt flow, with a cantilevered viewing platform.

hamilton-victoria-4.name: Mount Rouse
hamilton-victoria-4.bio: Extinct volcano at Penshurst with a crater lake walk and a summit platform looking to the Grampians.

horsham-1.name: Mount Arapiles
horsham-1.bio: Rock-climbing monolith (Dyurrite) rising from the Wimmera Plain, with a 1 km summit walk and panoramic views.

horsham-2.name: Pink Lake Dimboola
horsham-2.bio: Small salt lake near Dimboola that turns pink from algae, most striking after rain and white in long dry heat.

horsham-3.name: The Stick Shed
horsham-3.bio: Murtoa's 1941 emergency wheat store, the last of its type, with a cathedral-like forest of 560 timber poles.

horsham-4.name: Murtoa Silo Art
horsham-4.bio: Silo mural by SMUG at Murtoa honouring Dr John Cade, who discovered the effect of lithium on mental illness.

horsham-5.name: Rupanyup Silo Art
horsham-5.bio: Silo mural by Julia Volchkova showing Rupanyup's young people and their love of team sport.

horsham-6.name: Arkona Silo Art
horsham-6.bio: Silo mural of local man Roley Klinge on the Dimboola-Rainbow Road, celebrating country tennis.

little-desert-national-park.name: Little Desert National Park
little-desert-national-park.bio: Wimmera Mallee park of 132,647 hectares with walks of 30 minutes to three days and wildflowers from late winter.

budj-bim-national-park.name: Budj Bim National Park
budj-bim-national-park.bio: Volcanic park with a crater lake, lava canals and caves, co-managed with Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners.

lake-surprise.name: Lake Surprise
lake-surprise.bio: Crater lake in Budj Bim National Park, walkable from the campground, with a lava canal circuit past Tunnel Cave.

lower-glenelg-national-park.name: Lower Glenelg National Park
lower-glenelg-national-park.bio: Glenelg River gorge cut through limestone, with riverside camping, canoeing and part of the Great South West Walk.

princess-margaret-rose-caves.name: Princess Margaret Rose Caves
princess-margaret-rose-caves.bio: Show cave in Lower Glenelg National Park, 150 m long, with cave coral, rimstone pools and saw-toothed shawls.

tower-hill-wildlife-reserve.name: Tower Hill Wildlife Reserve
tower-hill-wildlife-reserve.bio: Dormant volcano crater near Warrnambool where emus, kangaroos and koalas live, with walks to the peak.

lake-bullen-merri.name: Lake Bullen Merri
lake-bullen-merri.bio: Brackish volcanic crater lake near Camperdown, about 66 m deep, paired with neighbouring Lake Gnotuk.

lake-gnotuk.name: Lake Gnotuk
lake-gnotuk.bio: Hypersaline crater lake near Camperdown, about twice as salty as seawater, beside Lake Bullen Merri.

colac-victoria.name: Colac
colac-victoria.bio: Western District town on the southern shore of Lake Colac, about 150 km south-west of Melbourne.

kara-kara-national-park.name: Kara Kara National Park
kara-kara-national-park.bio: Box-Ironbark park south of St Arnaud with 275 native plant species, ridge lookouts and a 2.8 km reservoir walk.

brim-silo-art.name: Brim Silo Art
brim-silo-art.bio: Guido van Helten's farmers on four 1939 silos, Victoria's first silo artwork and the Silo Art Trail's inspiration.

rainbow-silo-art.name: Rainbow Silo Art
rainbow-silo-art.bio: Geoffrey Carran's art on a 28 m silo with a lookout tower and internal light art reached by lift or stairs.

rosebery-silo-art.name: Rosebery Silo Art
rosebery-silo-art.bio: Kaff-eine's mural on 1939 GrainCorp silos, inspired by the local Mallee environment, on the Silo Art Trail.

sea-lake-silo-art.name: Sea Lake Silo Art
sea-lake-silo-art.bio: Silo mural of a girl swinging from a Mallee eucalypt, looking over Lake Tyrrell, on the Silo Art Trail.

patchewollock-silo-art.name: Patchewollock Silo Art
patchewollock-silo-art.bio: Fintan Magee's 2016 portrait of farmer Nick 'Noodle' Hulland on 35 m silos, the town's most notable feature.

goroke-silo-art.name: Goroke Silo Art
goroke-silo-art.bio: Geoffrey Carran's endangered birds painted on silos among gums, about an hour from Horsham.

lascelles-silo-art.name: Lascelles Silo Art
lascelles-silo-art.bio: Rone's 2017 monochrome portrait of farmers Geoff and Merrilyn Horman on two 1939 silos.

nulawil-silo-art.name: Nullawil Silo Art
nulawil-silo-art.bio: Sam Bates's photo-realistic farmer in a flannelette shirt with his kelpie, painted on the Nullawil silo.

serviceton-silo-art.name: Serviceton Silo Art
serviceton-silo-art.bio: Jack Fran's silo mural of the surveyors in the South Australia-Victoria border dispute, beside a grand railway station.

woomelang-silo-art.name: Woomelang Silo Art
woomelang-silo-art.bio: Eight small field-bin murals around town celebrate the Mallee's endangered species, with a carpark and picnic area.

sheep-hills-silo-art.name: Sheep Hills Silo Art
sheep-hills-silo-art.bio: Stop on the Silo Art Trail, a series of large murals on grain silos linking Wimmera Mallee towns.

st-arnaud-silo-art-and-murals.name: St Arnaud Silo Art and Murals
st-arnaud-silo-art-and-murals.bio: Silo and town murals in St Arnaud, near the Wimmera Mallee's Silo Art Trail of large-scale grain silo murals.

held.reason: Billimina Rock Art Site is reported closed to visitors after bushfire track damage
